Replication of PerSemCom (Tan et al., IEEE TCOM 2026) · Hindi

Personalized semantic speech transmission, in Hindi

The system sends the meaning of speech (its words) over a noisy radio channel instead of the sound itself, then re-speaks those words at the receiver in the original speaker's voice. Trained and tested on IndicVoices-R Hindi: 72 hours from 376 speakers.

Speech→Encoder→Noisy channel→Text decoder→Hindi corrector→Voice synthesis + speaker profile→Speech

Four results

78%of words survive heavy noise

At −2 dB SNR, 78% of words arrive correctly, against 80% for the same recogniser with no channel at all.

No cliffIt degrades gradually

At 2 dB and below, conventional digital links deliver nothing. PerSemCom still gets 50% of words through at −10 dB.

22.6×less bandwidth than a voice codec

795 channel symbols per second of speech, against 17,940 for AMR-WB with LDPC coding.

96%sounds like the right speaker

A speaker-ID model matches the re-spoken voice to the original speaker 96% of the time. Without the speaker profile: 8%.

Words received correctly as the channel gets worse

PerSemCom (semantic) Digital link: same text sent with LDPC coding

Steady noise (AWGN)

Fading channel (Rayleigh)

Test split, 1,326 sentences (3.6 h). Words correct = 100 − word error rate, after the corrector. Lower SNR means a noisier channel. Both systems start from the same recogniser, so they meet at the top.

Show the numbers

Hindi examples

Four test sentences, each from a different speaker. Each row shows what the receiver read at that channel condition, and the button plays the speech it re-created in the speaker's voice. Highlighted words differ from the transcript. Missing words show only in the count.

Spelling variants such as अधिकारिक / आधिकारिक and राष्ट्र भाषा / राष्ट्रभाषा count as errors here, so some “errors” at 10 dB are not real mistakes.

Against the paper

holds Reproduced in Hindi

  • Accuracy falls gradually with SNR, with no cliff.
  • The corrector helps most at low SNR.
  • A model trained on fading copes with steady noise, but not the other way round.
  • The speaker profile is what makes the voice personal.
  • It uses far fewer channel symbols than a codec.

partly Not yet matched

  • Speech quality. The re-created voice is less clear than real speech. A recogniser gets about 55% of its words right, against 79% for the AMR-WB codec at good SNR.
  • Even from a perfect transcript, our Tacotron 2 voice reaches only 58%. Voice synthesis is the bottleneck, not the channel.
Hardware: one RTX A2000 (12 GB). End-to-end latency 0.85 s for a 6.7 s sentence. Changes from the paper: a 1,000-piece vocabulary (5,000 collapsed on 65 h of data), a fine-tuned IndicBART corrector, an MMSE equaliser and Tacotron 2 with r = 3.
